keyword: blue origin new glenn rocket launch
claims: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket launched its third mission NG-3 on April 19, 2026, from Cape Canaveral.
The first-stage booster of NG-3 successfully completed its first reflight and landing.
The upper stage of NG-3 failed to place the AST SpaceMobile BlueBird 7 satellite into the correct orbit.
NG-3 lifted off at 7:25 a.m. EDT (11:25 UTC) from Launch Complex 36.
The goal of NG-3 was to deploy the AST SpaceMobile BlueBird 7 satellite into low Earth orbit.
The AST SpaceMobile BlueBird 7 satellite is designed for direct-to-smartphone broadband.
The first-stage booster of NG-3 is nicknamed "Never Tell Me The Odds".
The upper stage of NG-3 malfunctioned.
The upper stage of NG-3 placed the payload into a lower-than-planned orbit.
New Glenn is 322 feet tall (98 meters).
New Glenn completed its second flight in November 2025.
New Glenn's first stage uses seven BE-4 methane-fueled engines.
New Glenn's second stage is powered by two BE-3U hydrogen engines.
